title: Trust region and cubic regularization methods

items.title: Quadratic trust-region models and the actual-to-predicted reduction ratio
items.statement: Define the quadratic model m(p)=f(x)+gᵀp+½pᵀBp on the Euclidean ball ||p||₂≤Δ, its predicted and actual reductions, and their ratio when predicted reduction is positive.

items.title: The cubic-regularized quadratic model
The natural logarithm is bounded above by its positive argument minus one
items.statement: For every real x>=1, prove 0<=log x<=x-1<=x.

items.title: Global trust-region minimizers satisfy the shifted-Hessian conditions, including the hard case
items.statement: For a real symmetric B and Δ>0, characterize every global minimizer of gᵀp+½pᵀBp on ||p||₂≤Δ by (B+λI)p=−g, B+λI positive semidefinite, λ≥0, and λ(Δ−||p||₂)=0; give and prove the singular hard-case construction.

items.title: The Cauchy step for a quadratic trust-region model
Positive-definite Newton and dogleg steps are well-defined
items.statement: For a symmetric positive-definite model matrix B, prove that B is invertible and that Bp=−g has a unique solution p for every g.

items.title: Global cubic minimizers, admissible inexact steps, and cubic Cauchy decrease
items.statement: For σ>0 and symmetric B, prove that the cubic model attains a global minimum and every nonstationary global minimizer s satisfies m(0)−m(s)≥σ||s||₂³/6.

items.title: The Cauchy step gives a quantitative model decrease
items.statement: For symmetric B, g≠0 and Δ>0, prove m(0)−m(p_C)≥½||g||₂ min{Δ,||g||₂/||B||₂}, with the zero-matrix convention stated explicitly.

items.title: Dogleg steps for positive-definite trust-region models
Truncated conjugate gradients with boundary and negative-curvature exits
Finite-budget adaptive regularization using cubic models
Truncated-CG iterates are feasible and lie in generated Krylov subspaces
items.statement: Before a boundary or curvature exit, prove z_j∈K_j(B,−g) and r_j,d_j∈K_{j+1}(B,−g) for the stated truncated-CG recurrence.

items.title: A finite-budget trust-region method with ratio-based radius updates
The actual-to-predicted ratio approaches one at small radii away from stationarity
items.statement: For an L-Lipschitz gradient, uniformly bounded model Hessians, and steps with a fixed fraction of Cauchy decrease, bound the ratio error and give an explicit radius below which ρ≥η₂ when ||g||₂≥ε.

items.title: Cubic regularization bounds consecutive unsuccessful trials
items.statement: Under the stated regularization floor and cap, exact-Hessian Lipschitz model, and multiplicative rejection update, bound rejected trials per successful trial by an explicit constant independent of ε.

items.title: Cauchy-decrease trust-region iterations have liminf gradient norm zero
items.statement: Under the stated bounded-model, Lipschitz-gradient, bounded-below, ratio-update, and Cauchy-decrease hypotheses, prove that the trust-region process terminates at a stationary point or liminfₖ||∇f(xₖ)||₂=0.

items.title: Trust-region first-order complexity counts both successful and unsuccessful trials
items.statement: For the target-aware assumptions and radius-update rules stated, prove O(ε⁻²) accepted steps and O(ε⁻²) total trials to reach ||∇f(x)||₂≤ε, including an explicit telescoping bound for rejected trials.

items.title: Adaptive cubic regularization reaches first-order accuracy in O(ε⁻³ᐟ²) evaluations
items.statement: Under a Lipschitz Hessian, lower-bounded objective, exact global cubic-model steps, and the stated regularization/update conditions, prove O(ε⁻³ᐟ²) accepted steps and total function-and-gradient evaluations to reach ||∇f(x)||₂≤ε.

title: Trust region and cubic regularization methods — Examples

items.title: An indefinite quadratic has a unique boundary trust-region minimizer
items.statement: Compute the global minimizer and multiplier for B=diag(−1,1), g=(−1,−3)/√2, and Δ=1; verify the shifted-Hessian conditions and compare its predicted decrease with the Cauchy step.

items.title: A singular shifted Hessian produces two hard-case minimizers
items.statement: For B=diag(−2,1), g=(0,1), and Δ=1, compute both global minimizers, their common model value, and the singular multiplier λ=2.

items.title: Newton, Cauchy, and truncated-CG steps on one indefinite model
items.statement: For B=diag(−1,1), g=(−1,−3)/√2, and Δ=1, compute the raw Newton direction, Cauchy step, and first truncated-CG boundary exit; verify model reductions and the exact descent safeguard imported from the inexact-Newton algorithm.
